sections.html:
McKinley County lies in the northwest corner of New Mexico against the Arizona line. Gallup is the county seat and the only incorporated city. The 2020 census counted 72,902 residents, with 21,899 in Gallup and 2,900 in Crownpoint. That leaves 48,103 people spread across rural communities such as Thoreau, Tohatchi, Church Rock, Ramah, Pinehaven and Zuni Pueblo.

Over 60 percent of the county's land is part of the Navajo Nation or the Zuni Reservation. Median home value is $72,100, well below the state midpoint, so bills here run smaller in dollars, though the penalty rules are the same as anywhere else in the state. For most properties, the first job is pinning down which jurisdiction the parcel sits in.

sections.h2: Fee land, trust land and what you can sell
sections.html:
Land status decides which rules apply. Trust land inside the reservations is not subject to state or local taxes, though tribes may tax it to fund their own services. The Navajo Nation also levies a possessory interest tax on the right to use Navajo land for something like an oil and gas lease, a right-of-way or a business site lease. Fee land, ordinary privately owned land with a deed, stays under county rules.

  • Fee land with a recorded deed is assessed by the McKinley County Assessor and billed by the Treasurer.
  • Trust land and tribal land assignments follow tribal and federal procedures.
  • Before you price or advertise, find out whether your land is fee, trust, or held by lease or assignment.

The assessor's records and the county clerk's recorded documents are the quickest way to tell fee land from other holdings. A title company will ask the same thing first.

The McKinley County Assessor lists and values taxable property. The McKinley County Treasurer collects taxes, penalties and interest under the Property Tax Code, Sections 7-35-1 through 7-38-90 NMSA 1978.

County TreasurerCollects property tax, manages county funds207 W Hill Ave, Suite 101, Gallup, NM 87301; (505) 722-4459; 8 AM to 5 PM, Monday to Friday

The county posts charts of taxes billed by taxing entity for each tax year, which show how one bill divides among county, school and other districts. Start at the treasurer's page and the assessor's page.

McKinley County follows the statewide calendar, with payments due November 10 and April 10.

  • January 1: property is valued as of this date, and the tax lien attaches.
  • September 1: the state Department of Finance and Administration sets rates.
  • November 1: treasurers send bills.
  • November 10 and December 10: the first half is due, and interest starts after December 10.
  • April 10 and May 10: the second half is due, and interest starts after May 10.
  • January 10 of the following year: last day to file a refund claim in district court.

Late interest runs at 1 percent a month. The lien is a first lien under Section 7-38-48, ahead of any other interest, so an unpaid McKinley County bill follows the house to whoever owns it next.

The assessor values a home at current and correct value as of January 1, and taxable value is one third of that figure. Residential assessments cannot climb more than 3 percent a year unless the property changes ownership, is improved or is rezoned.

Two points matter in a sale. A change of ownership lifts the cap, so the buyer's first valuation is a fresh one. And the $2,000 head of family exemption belongs to a resident's primary home and is removed when ownership changes. A transfer to a child who occupies the home as a principal residence, or into a revocable trust for the owner's spouse or child, does not count as a change of ownership.

sections.h2: How to appeal a high valuation
sections.html:
File a written petition with the assessor within 30 days of the mailing of the notice of valuation, or by April 1, whichever is later. A county valuation protest board hears it, and one seat on that board goes to a member of the state's Appraisal Bureau.

A timely protest keeps the disputed part of the tax from becoming delinquent. The alternative is to pay first and file a refund claim in district court. There is no fee for an initial protest, and the state department publishes a protest pamphlet.

After three full years of delinquency, the account moves to the state's Delinquent Property Tax Bureau, which can sell the property at public auction. Before that, the bureau tries phone calls, certified mail, site visits and notices left on the property, and it offers installment agreements.

If an auction brings in more than the tax, penalty, interest and costs, the former owner gets the difference. The state must hold an auction in each county every year, and McKinley is no exception.

  • Heirs who inherit a house on fee land should look at the treasurer's account before listing.
  • Owners who moved away should confirm the treasurer has a current mailing address.

sections.h2: How a quick sale usually goes
sections.html:
The seller proves ownership, clears any tax lien, and signs a deed that is recorded with the county clerk. Under Section 14-9-3 NMSA 1978, an unrecorded deed does not affect title against a later purchaser, so recording is what protects the buyer.

If an estate is attached to the house, probate comes first. An estate that includes real property cannot use the small-estate affidavit, and a personal representative's deed may be needed to move title out of the decedent's name.

A workable sequence: confirm the land is fee land, pull the treasurer's payoff, settle any probate step, then sign and record the deed. A cash buyer who closes as-is will usually handle the rest.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in McKinley County, NM?
faqs.a: The McKinley County Treasurer, at 207 W Hill Ave, Suite 101, in Gallup, phone (505) 722-4459. The office is open 8 AM to 5 PM, Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: When are McKinley County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 10 for the first half and April 10 for the second. Interest starts after December 10 and May 10.

faqs.q: Is trust land in McKinley County taxed by the county?
faqs.a: No. Trust land is not subject to state or local taxes. Tribes may assess their own taxes, such as the Navajo possessory interest tax.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest my valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date the assessor mailed the notice, or until April 1, whichever is later. File the petition with the county assessor.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McKinley County house that has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax has to be paid or settled at closing, because the lien ranks ahead of other interests. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer.
